confidence: Low. Motives are now abundant; Hugh and Monet have especially severe stakes, while Chip and Brie retain plausible means connections. Statements alone cannot establish innocence or guilt.
plausibility_notes: Each confession is understandable individually, with shades of responsibility and coercion.
All thirty confess wrongdoing followed by a Grant grievance in nearly identical structure; collectively this feels engineered to supply universal motive.
Grant appears to have blackmailed or coerced nearly everyone at the same event, which strains ordinary behavior even within party conventions.
Artie accepting another job legitimately reduces the initial forced-resignation hook.
No confession by itself establishes the physical murder sequence.
